title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 12 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Angles' test?
options: A geometric property based on number of sides
Whether a group of shapes share a common angle-based property (all right angles, all acute, etc.)
A material-based property
A biological property
questions.rationale: This tests whether shapes share a common angle-based property, identifying the shape whose angles differ from the shared pattern.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Number of Diagonals' test?
options: A material-based property
Whether a group of polygons share the same number of diagonals, with one polygon having a different count
A biological property
A use-based property
questions.rationale: Using the diagonal-count formula, this tests whether polygons share the same number of diagonals, identifying the one whose diagonal count differs.

questions.question: What does 'Classification by Symmetry' test?
options: A material-based property
Whether a group of shapes share a common symmetry property (line symmetry, rotational symmetry, etc.), with one lacking it
A use-based property
A biological property
questions.rationale: This tests whether shapes share a common symmetry property, identifying the shape that lacks the same kind of symmetry.

questions.question: What does 'Non-Verbal Classification' refer to?
options: Classification based only on word meaning
Classification based on visual/figural properties (shapes, patterns) rather than words or numbers
Classification based only on numbers
A classification method with no visual component
questions.rationale: Non-verbal classification is based on visual or figural properties — shapes and patterns — rather than word-based or purely numeric reasoning.

questions.question: What is a 'Shape Feature Vector'?
options: A vector with no shape-related data
A representation of a shape's key measurable features (sides, angles, symmetry, etc.) used to compare shapes systematically
A vector only for numbers
A vector unrelated to classification
questions.rationale: A shape feature vector captures a shape's key measurable properties, enabling systematic comparison to identify the shape that differs from the rest.

questions.question: What does the 'Non-Verbal Classification Workflow' likely provide?
options: A random guessing method
A systematic step-by-step process specifically for identifying the odd shape/figure out among a set of visual figures
A workflow only for word classification
A workflow with no defined steps
questions.rationale: This provides a systematic, step-by-step process tailored specifically to solving non-verbal (figural) classification problems.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'Rotation' and 'Reflection' in non-verbal classification?
options: They are the same transformation
A rotation turns a figure around a point (preserving its arrangement), while a reflection mirrors it (reversing the arrangement)
Reflection is just a synonym for rotation
Neither transformation is relevant to classification
questions.rationale: A rotation turns a figure around a point while preserving its internal arrangement, while a reflection mirrors the figure, reversing that arrangement — a key distinction when comparing figures.

questions.question: What does the 'Counting Method' apply to non-verbal classification?
options: Ignoring the number of elements entirely
Counting specific elements (like sides, dots, or shapes) within each figure to find the one with a different count
Only measuring angles
Only checking colors
questions.rationale: The counting method compares the count of specific elements (sides, dots, sub-shapes) within each figure, identifying the one whose count differs.

questions.question: What does the 'Position Method' check for in non-verbal classification?
options: The color of each figure
Whether elements within each figure are positioned consistently (e.g., always in the same relative spot), with one figure breaking that pattern
Only the size of each figure
Only the number of sides
questions.rationale: The position method checks whether the internal elements of each figure are consistently positioned relative to each other, identifying the figure that breaks that positional consistency.

questions.question: What does the 'Orientation Method' check for?
options: The color of each figure
Whether each figure is consistently oriented (facing the same direction or rotated the same way), with one breaking that pattern
Only the size of each figure
Only the number of elements
questions.rationale: The orientation method checks whether figures share a consistent facing direction or rotation, identifying the figure oriented differently from the rest.
